section.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains why Chanukah lights differ from the Temple menorah in their lighting time, specifically at sunset, because the revelation of the level of Yechidah, which transcends the chain of descent, illuminates even the darkness and transforms it into light.
section.t: And this is also the reason that the Chanukah lights are distinct from the lights of the Temple also in the time of their lighting,
that the mitzvah of Chanukah lights is from sunset,
for specifically through the revelation
(of the aspect of Yechidah)
which is above the chain of descent
(in man),
they also illuminate the darkness.
For not only is the darkness unable to conceal before this light,
but moreover,
the darkness is transformed into light.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the time limit for Chanukah lights until the foot of the Tarmudai ceases from the market, explaining that the light of Chanukah both annihilates the rebellious Tarmudai and also brings them to a state of soul-longing.
section.t: And this is also that the time of Chanukah lights is until the foot ceases from the market, until the foot of the Tarmudai ceases,
Tarmudai are those who rebel against the kingdom of Heaven
(Tarmud is the letters of Moredet [rebellious])
and they linger in the market
the aspect of the public domain, mountains of separation,
and through Chanukah lights there is a cessation of the foot of the Tarmudai,
there being two explanations of this.
That the light of Chanukah consumes and nullifies the foot of the Tarmudai,
and that the light of Chanukah effects a cessation
(cession from the term "consumption" and "soul-longing")
also in the foot of the Tarmudai,
that even the rebels will come to the aspect of soul-longing.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between Chanukah lights and Sukkot and the seventy bulls of the festival, showing how both involve eight days, the drawing down of the transcendent One into the seven of the chain of descent, and the transformation of the nations from opposition to assistance.
section.t: And based on all the above, the difference between Chanukah lights and Sukkot and the fruits of the festival will be understood,
for the matter of Sukkot
(and also the matter of the fruits of the festival)
is the revelation of the encompassing lights,
analogous to the simple sukkah which encompasses a person.
And on the Eighth of Sukkot, the encompassing lights are drawn down and are also internalized within the interior,
analogous to the service of self-nullification
(of Chanukah)
which effects
(as above)
and penetrates all the powers of the soul.
And this is that both of them
(Sukkot and Chanukah)
are eight days,
for the number eight is one and seven,
that the one
(which is above the chain of descent)
is drawn into the seven
(the chain of descent).
And just as Chanukah lights effect also in the foot of the Tarmudai in two matters,
that initially it consumes and nullifies them and afterwards it effects in them that they too are transformed into holiness,
so too is it regarding the offering of the seventy bulls of the festival corresponding to the seventy nations of the world,
that initially the offering effects that the nations diminish and decrease,
and afterwards it effects in them that they too assist Israel,
as the Sages said,
"If the nations of the world knew how beneficial the Temple was for them, they would surround it with legions
to guard it, etc."
For through effecting in them the matter of transformation,
there is added through them assistance
(also)
in holiness,
the guarding of the Temple.
And analogous to how it will be in the future,
when "I will then transform the peoples, etc., to serve Him with one accord,"
then "strangers will stand and shepherd your flocks."
And analogous to the offering of the seventy bulls corresponding to the seventy nations,
and to the point that through and from the side of the nations there is added
(on the Eighth)
an offering for the children of Israel in the Holy Temple.
